stem: Find algebraically, by omitting one variable, the solution of the two equations ${=a}x+{=b}y={=c}$ (1) and ${=d}x-{=e}y={=f}$ (2). Write the answer as an ordered pair $(x, y)$.
solution: To omit $y$, multiply (1) by ${=e}$ and (2) by ${=b}$: ${=a*e}x + {=b*e}y = {=c*e}$ (3) and ${=b*d}x - {=b*e}y = {=b*f}$ (4).
The solution is $({=x0}, {=y0})$, and the two equations have exactly one solution.
notes: Advanced: both equations must be multiplied; negative solutions and a negative right-hand side possible. Determinant -(ae+bd) is never zero so always exactly one solution.
